newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-RIVAL COACHES MEET AT TOURNAMENT LAUNCH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RIVAL COACHES MEET AT TOURNAMENT LAUNCH.

text.p: Glenn Hoddle and Cesare Maldini's meeting in Paris on Thursday will be easily the friendliest of their four scheduled for 1997.
The England and Italy coaches, whose sides clash in two World Cup qualifiers this year, were at the presentation of a four-team warm-up tournament in France in June in which they also meet.

They were joined by Mario Zagalo of Brazil and France's Aime Jacquet, who as coaches of holders and host country, do not have to get their teams through qualifiers but are desperate for all the competition they can find.
The round-robin Tournament de France consists of six matches between June 3 and 11. The winners of each match will earn five million francs ($1 million) in prize money.
Former France captain Michel Platini, co-chief of the World Cup organising committee, said the tournament would be as full a dress rehearsal as possible at five of the 10 venues for the 1998 finals.

"The draw for the World Cup qualifiers had not yet been made when France invited England and Italy to take part," Platini said. The two countries were subsequently drawn in group two which England currently lead.
"We have no problem meeting Italy in the tournament. Obviously we have to qualify for the World Cup, but it's a rehearsal and we would like to win the tournament," Hoddle said.
The newly-appointed Maldini makes his debut as a World Cup coach when he takes Italy to Wembley for their first qualifying clash with England on February 12.
Their meeting on June 4 in Nantes in the second match of the Tournament de France could have a significant bearing on their final and potentially crucial encounter in Italy on October 11.
Maldini said: "They are two totally different matches. (In the tournament) we'll be conscious of the teams strengths."

Zagalo, meanwhile, is bracing himself for a tug-of-war with the big Spanish clubs over the release of his many players in Spain's first division championship whose decisive final days coincide with the tournament in France.

"I hope to put out my strongest team. I have the right to call up those (Spain-based) players. There is a clause in their contracts when they sign for Spanish clubs that they must be released for the national team," Zagalo said.
"With Brazil not taking part in qualifiers, I need to have the best competition as I rebuild the national team. I have the Copa America right afterwards."
Zagalo indicated that the standard of Brazil's rivals in the Tournament of France might constitute a better yardstick for the strength of his side.
But it would be easier to bring together a full strength squad for the Copa America, an official event, in Bolivia in the second half of June.
France's Aime Jacquet faces the same problems as Zagalo, with no qualifiers to steel his players and several members of his squad in the Spanish first division.
But he said: "We have good relations with the big Spanish clubs and so far we have not had any problems."
Schedule of matches for the tournament:
June 3 - France v Brazil, in Lyon
June 4 - Italy v England, Nantes
June 7 - France v England, Montpellier
June 8 - Brazil v Italy, Lyon
June 10 - England v Brazil, Lens
June 11 - France v Italy, Paris
